exercises.title: GitHub Actions Workflow con Claude Code
exercises.instructions: Crea un workflow completo de GitHub Actions que integre Claude Code para automatizar code review y testing.

config.challenge:
Diseña e implementa un workflow de GitHub Actions que:

**Requisitos:**
1. Se ejecute en cada Pull Request
2. Instale Claude Code en el runner
3. Ejecute análisis de código automático
4. Genere comentarios en el PR con hallazgos
5. Falle el workflow si hay issues críticos
6. Genere reporte de coverage y calidad

**Componentes necesarios:**
- Workflow YAML (.github/workflows/claude-review.yml)
- Script de integración (scripts/claude-ci.sh)
- Configuración de Claude Code para CI
- Template de comentarios para PR

**Bonus (5 pts extra):**
- Implementar caching de dependencias
- Usar matrix strategy para múltiples versiones de Node
- Integrar con GitHub Checks API

**Entrega:**
1. Archivo workflow completo
2. Scripts auxiliares necesarios
3. Ejemplo de output esperado en PR
config.solution:
# Archivo: .github/workflows/claude-review.yml

```yaml
name: Claude Code Review

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
    branches:
      - main
      - develop

env:
  NODE_VERSION: '18.x'

jobs:
  claude-analysis:
    name: AI-Powered Code Review
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15

    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
      checks: write

    steps:
      # 1. Checkout código
      - name: Checkout PR code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0  # Historia completa para análisis
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}

      # 2. Setup Node.js con caching
      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: 'npm'

      # 3. Instalar dependencias
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          npm ci --prefer-offline --no-audit
          npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

      # 4. Configurar Claude Code
      - name: Configure Claude Code
        env:
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p ~/.config/claude-code
          cat > ~/.config/claude-code/config.json <<EOF
          {
            "model": "claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022",
            "maxTokens": 4096,
            "headless": true,
            "ci": true,
            "outputFormat": "json"
          }
          EOF

      # 5. Obtener archivos modificados
      - name: Get changed files
        id: changed-files
        run: |
          # Comparar con base branch
          BASE_SHA=${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA=${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          
          CHANGED_FILES=$(git diff --name-only $BASE_SHA $HEAD_SHA | grep -E '\.(ts|js|tsx|jsx)$' || true)
          
          echo "Changed files:"
          echo "$CHANGED_FILES"
          
          # Guardar para siguientes steps
          echo "files<<EOF" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "$CHANGED_FILES" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "EOF" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      # 6. Ejecutar análisis con Claude Code
      - name: Run Claude Code Analysis
        id: claude-analysis
        env:
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          chmod +x ./scripts/claude-ci.sh
          ./scripts/claude-ci.sh "${{ steps.changed-files.outputs.files }}"
        continue-on-error: true

      # 7. Parsear resultados
      - name: Parse analysis results
        id: parse-results
        run: |
          if [ -f claude-report.json ]; then
            CRITICAL=$(jq -r '.issues[] | select(.severity=="critical") | .title' claude-report.json | wc -l)
            HIGH=$(jq -r '.issues[] | select(.severity=="high") | .title' claude-report.json | wc -l)
            MEDIUM=$(jq -r '.issues[] | select(.severity=="medium") | .title' claude-report.json | wc -l)
            
            echo "critical=$CRITICAL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "high=$HIGH" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "medium=$MEDIUM" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            
            # Determinar si debe fallar
            if [ "$CRITICAL" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "should_fail=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            else
              echo "should_fail=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            fi
          else
            echo "No report generated"
            exit 1
          fi

      # 8. Generar comentario en PR
      - name: Comment PR
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const fs = require('fs');
            const report = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('claude-report.json', 'utf8'));
            
            // Construir comentario
            let comment = `## 🤖 Claude Code Review\n\n`;
            comment += `**Análisis completado en:** ${report.duration}s\n`;
            comment += `**Archivos analizados:** ${report.filesAnalyzed}\n\n`;
            
            // Summary
            comment += `### 📊 Resumen\n\n`;
            comment += `- 🔴 Critical: ${report.summary.critical}\n`;
            comment += `- 🟠 High: ${report.summary.high}\n`;
            comment += `- 🟡 Medium: ${report.summary.medium}\n`;
            comment += `- 🟢 Low: ${report.summary.low}\n\n`;
            
            // Critical issues (detalle)
            if (report.summary.critical > 0) {
              comment += `### 🔴 Issues Críticos\n\n`;
              report.issues
                .filter(i => i.severity === 'critical')
                .forEach(issue => {
                  comment += `#### ${issue.title}\n`;
                  comment += `**File:** \`${issue.file}:${issue.line}\`\n`;
                  comment += `**Description:** ${issue.description}\n`;
                  comment += `**Fix:**\n\`\`\`${issue.language || 'typescript'}\n${issue.suggestedFix}\n\`\`\`\n\n`;
                });
            }
            
            // High issues (solo títulos)
            if (report.summary.high > 0) {
              comment += `### 🟠 Issues de Alta Prioridad\n\n`;
              report.issues
                .filter(i => i.severity === 'high')
                .forEach(issue => {
                  comment += `- **${issue.title}** - \`${issue.file}:${issue.line}\`\n`;
                });
              comment += `\n`;
            }
            
            // Recommendations
            if (report.recommendations && report.recommendations.length > 0) {
              comment += `### 💡 Recomendaciones\n\n`;
              report.recommendations.forEach(rec => {
                comment += `- ${rec}\n`;
              });
            }
            
            // Footer
            comment += `\n---\n`;
            comment += `*Powered by Claude Code | [View full report](${process.env.GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${process.env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${process.env.GITHUB_RUN_ID})*`;
            
            // Post comment
            await github.rest.issues.createComment({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
              body: comment
            });

      # 9. Crear check
      - name: Create Check
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const fs = require('fs');
            const report = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('claude-report.json', 'utf8'));
            
            const conclusion = report.summary.critical > 0 ? 'failure' : 'success';
            const summary = `Found ${report.summary.critical} critical, ${report.summary.high} high, ${report.summary.medium} medium issues`;
            
            await github.rest.checks.create({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              name: 'Claude Code Analysis',
              head_sha: context.payload.pull_request.head.sha,
              status: 'completed',
              conclusion: conclusion,
              output: {
                title: 'AI Code Review',
                summary: summary,
                text: JSON.stringify(report, null, 2)
              }
            });

      # 10. Fallar si hay issues críticos
      - name: Fail if critical issues
        if: steps.parse-results.outputs.should_fail == 'true'
        run: |
          echo "❌ Found critical issues. Please fix before merging."
          exit 1

      # 11. Upload report como artifact
      - name: Upload report
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: claude-code-report
          path: |
            claude-report.json
            claude-full-log.txt
          retention-days: 30
```

# Archivo: scripts/claude-ci.sh

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

CHANGED_FILES="$1"

echo "🤖 Starting Claude Code CI Analysis..."
echo ""

# Verificar que hay archivos para analizar
if [ -z "$CHANGED_FILES" ]; then
  echo "No files to analyze. Skipping."
  echo '{"filesAnalyzed": 0, "issues": [], "summary": {"critical": 0, "high": 0, "medium": 0, "low": 0}}' > claude-report.json
  exit 0
fi

# Crear prompt para Claude
cat > analysis-prompt.txt <<EOF
Analyze the following files for:
1. Security vulnerabilities (SQL injection, XSS, hardcoded secrets)
2. Code quality issues (complexity, duplication, bad patterns)
3. Performance problems
4. Best practices violations
5. Type safety issues

For each issue found, provide:
- Severity: critical/high/medium/low
- File and line number
- Clear description
- Suggested fix with code

Files to analyze:
$CHANGED_FILES

Output format: JSON with structure:
{
  "filesAnalyzed": number,
  "duration": number (seconds),
  "issues": [
    {
      "severity": "critical|high|medium|low",
      "title": "Issue title",
      "file": "path/to/file.ts",
      "line": number,
      "description": "Detailed description",
      "suggestedFix": "Fixed code",
      "language": "typescript"
    }
  ],
  "summary": {
    "critical": number,
    "high": number,
    "medium": number,
    "low": number
  },
  "recommendations": ["General recommendations"]
}
EOF

# Ejecutar Claude Code
START_TIME=$(date +%s)

claude --headless < analysis-prompt.txt > claude-raw-output.txt 2>&1 || true

END_TIME=$(date +%s)
DURATION=$((END_TIME - START_TIME))

# Extraer JSON del output (Claude puede incluir texto adicional)
grep -o '{.*}' claude-raw-output.txt | tail -1 > claude-report.json || {
  # Si no hay JSON válido, crear reporte de error
  echo "⚠️  Failed to parse Claude output"
  echo '{"filesAnalyzed": 0, "issues": [], "summary": {"critical": 0, "high": 0, "medium": 0, "low": 0}, "error": "Failed to analyze"}' > claude-report.json
  exit 1
}

# Agregar duration al report
jq ". + {duration: $DURATION}" claude-report.json > tmp.json && mv tmp.json claude-report.json

# Guardar log completo
cp claude-raw-output.txt claude-full-log.txt

echo ""
echo "✅ Analysis complete!"
jq -r '.summary | "Critical: \(.critical), High: \(.high), Medium: \(.medium), Low: \(.low)"' claude-report.json
```

# Ejemplo de Output en PR:

```markdown
## 🤖 Claude Code Review

**Análisis completado en:** 23s
**Archivos analizados:** 8

### 📊 Resumen

- 🔴 Critical: 2
- 🟠 High: 5
- 🟡 Medium: 8
- 🟢 Low: 3

### 🔴 Issues Críticos

#### SQL Injection Vulnerability
**File:** `src/api/users.controller.ts:45`
**Description:** Direct string concatenation in SQL query allows injection attacks
**Fix:**
```typescript
// ❌ Vulnerable
const query = `SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '${email}'`;

// ✅ Secure
const query = 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?';
const result = await db.query(query, [email]);
```

#### Hardcoded API Key
**File:** `src/config/stripe.ts:12`
**Description:** Stripe API key is hardcoded in source code
**Fix:**
```typescript
// ❌ Hardcoded
const stripe = new Stripe('sk_live_51H...');

// ✅ Environment variable
const stripe = new Stripe(process.env.STRIPE_API_KEY!);
```

### 🟠 Issues de Alta Prioridad

- **Missing Input Validation** - `src/api/auth.controller.ts:28`
- **Unhandled Promise Rejection** - `src/services/email.service.ts:67`
- **Weak Password Hashing** - `src/auth/password.util.ts:15`
- **Missing Error Boundaries** - `src/components/Dashboard.tsx:89`
- **Potential Memory Leak** - `src/hooks/useWebSocket.ts:34`

### 💡 Recomendaciones

- Implementar input validation con Zod o Joi en todos los endpoints
- Agregar rate limiting para prevenir ataques de fuerza bruta
- Configurar ESLint con plugins de seguridad
- Implementar logging centralizado para auditoría

---
*Powered by Claude Code | [View full report](https://github.com/org/repo/actions/runs/123456789)*
```

exercises.title: Headless Mode y Scripting
exercises.instructions: Responde sobre el uso de Claude Code en modo headless para automatización.

questions.question: ¿Cuál es la principal diferencia entre modo interactivo y headless en Claude Code?
options: Headless no requiere intervención humana y puede ejecutarse en scripts/CI
questions.explanation: Headless mode permite ejecutar Claude Code sin interacción humana, perfecto para automatización en CI/CD pipelines, cron jobs, o scripts batch. El modo interactivo requiere que un humano esté presente para aprobar acciones.

questions.question: ¿Cómo se activa el modo headless en Claude Code?
questions.explanation: Se puede activar con el flag --headless en la CLI o configurando la variable de entorno CLAUDE_HEADLESS=true. Esto desactiva todos los prompts interactivos.

questions.question: En modo headless, ¿cómo se pasa el input a Claude Code?
options: Via stdin (pipe), archivos, o variables de entorno
questions.explanation: En headless mode, puedes pasar input via: stdin (echo 'prompt' | claude --headless), archivos (claude --headless < prompt.txt), o variables de entorno (CLAUDE_PROMPT='...' claude --headless).

questions.question: ¿Cuál es un caso de uso válido para headless mode?
options: Nightly batch job que genera reportes de calidad de código
questions.explanation: Headless mode es ideal para tareas automatizadas como: nightly jobs de análisis, generación automatizada de documentación, refactoring batch de múltiples repositorios, testing automatizado, etc.

questions.question: En headless mode, ¿cómo se maneja el output de Claude Code?
options: Se imprime siempre en la consola
Se puede redirigir a archivos, logs, o parsear con jq para JSON
questions.explanation: El output de headless mode va a stdout/stderr y puede ser redirigido a archivos, parseado (si usas --output-format json), o enviado a sistemas de logging. Ejemplo: claude --headless --output-format json < prompt.txt > result.json

exercises.title: Trabajo en Equipo con Claude Code
exercises.instructions: Empareja cada escenario de trabajo en equipo con la mejor práctica de Claude Code.

pairs.left: Onboarding de nuevo desarrollador al proyecto
pairs.right: Comando custom /onboard que genera tour del codebase + setup automático + tasks iniciales

pairs.left: Establecer estándares de código para todo el equipo
pairs.right: Subagent code-reviewer compartido en .claude/ con reglas del equipo

pairs.left: Compartir comandos útiles entre el equipo
pairs.right: Repositorio de slash commands en .claude/commands/ committeado en Git

pairs.left: Auditar quién usó Claude Code y qué cambios hizo
pairs.right: Hooks de logging centralizados que registran todas las operaciones

pairs.left: Prevenir que Claude modifique archivos críticos
pairs.right: Configuración managed-settings.json con reglas de escritura
Prompts MCP que generan ADRs (Architecture Decision Records) consistentes

config.explanation: Trabajar en equipo con Claude Code requiere: 1) Compartir configuración via Git, 2) Estandarizar workflows con comandos custom, 3) Auditar con hooks, 4) Proteger archivos críticos con policies, 5) Documentar decisiones consistentemente.

config.challenge:
Implementa una configuración completa de Claude Code con AWS Bedrock que incluya:

**Requisitos de Infraestructura:**
1. IAM Role con permisos mínimos necesarios (least privilege)
2. VPC Endpoint para Bedrock (sin internet pública)
3. CloudWatch Logs para auditoría
4. KMS encryption para datos en tránsito/reposo
5. Secrets Manager para API credentials

**Requisitos de Configuración:**
1. Terraform/CloudFormation para infrastructure as code
2. Claude Code config apuntando a Bedrock
3. Script de setup automatizado
4. Health check y monitoring
5. Disaster recovery plan

**Requisitos de Seguridad:**
1. Network isolation (private subnets)
2. Encryption at rest y in transit
3. Audit logging de todas las requests
4. Rate limiting y quotas
5. Compliance con SOC2/HIPAA

**Entrega:**
1. Archivos Terraform/CloudFormation
2. Claude Code configuration
3. Scripts de deployment
4. Documentación de arquitectura
5. Runbook operacional
config.solution:
# Parte 1: Terraform Infrastructure

## main.tf

```hcl
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.0"
  required_providers {
    aws = {
      source  = "hashicorp/aws"
      version = "~> 5.0"
    }
  }

  backend "s3" {
    bucket = "company-terraform-state"
    key    = "claude-code/bedrock/terraform.tfstate"
    region = "us-east-1"
    encrypt = true
  }
}

provider "aws" {
  region = var.aws_region

  default_tags {
    tags = {
      Project     = "ClaudeCode-Bedrock"
      Environment = var.environment
      ManagedBy   = "Terraform"
      CostCenter  = "Engineering"
    }
  }
}

# Variables
variable "aws_region" {
  description = "AWS region for Bedrock"
  type        = string
  default     = "us-east-1"
}

variable "environment" {
  description = "Environment (dev, staging, prod)"
  type        = string
}

variable "vpc_id" {
  description = "VPC ID for private networking"
  type        = string
}

variable "private_subnet_ids" {
  description = "Private subnet IDs for VPC endpoint"
  type        = list(string)
}

# KMS Key for encryption
resource "aws_kms_key" "bedrock" {
  description             = "KMS key for Claude Code Bedrock encryption"
  deletion_window_in_days = 30
  enable_key_rotation     = true

  policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17"
    Statement = [
      {
        Sid    = "Enable IAM User Permissions"
        Effect = "Allow"
        Principal = {
          AWS = "arn:aws:iam::${data.aws_caller_identity.current.account_id}:root"
        }
        Action   = "kms:*"
        Resource = "*"
      },
      {
        Sid    = "Allow Bedrock to use the key"
        Effect = "Allow"
        Principal = {
          Service = "bedrock.amazonaws.com"
        }
        Action = [
          "kms:Decrypt",
          "kms:GenerateDataKey"
        ]
        Resource = "*"
      }
    ]
  })
}

resource "aws_kms_alias" "bedrock" {
  name          = "alias/claude-code-bedrock-${var.environment}"
  target_key_id = aws_kms_key.bedrock.key_id
}

# VPC Endpoint for Bedrock (private access)
resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "bedrock_runtime" {
  vpc_id              = var.vpc_id
  service_name        = "com.amazonaws.${var.aws_region}.bedrock-runtime"
  vpc_endpoint_type   = "Interface"
  subnet_ids          = var.private_subnet_ids
  security_group_ids  = [aws_security_group.bedrock_endpoint.id]
  private_dns_enabled = true

  tags = {
    Name = "bedrock-runtime-endpoint-${var.environment}"
  }
}

# Security Group for VPC Endpoint
resource "aws_security_group" "bedrock_endpoint" {
  name_description = "Security group for Bedrock VPC endpoint"
  vpc_id          = var.vpc_id

  ingress {
    description = "HTTPS from VPC"
    from_port   = 443
    to_port     = 443
    protocol    = "tcp"
    cidr_blocks = [data.aws_vpc.main.cidr_block]
  }

  egress {
    description = "Allow all outbound"
    from_port   = 0
    to_port     = 0
    protocol    = "-1"
    cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
  }

  tags = {
    Name = "bedrock-endpoint-sg-${var.environment}"
  }
}

# IAM Role for Claude Code application
resource "aws_iam_role" "claude_code" {
  name = "claude-code-bedrock-role-${var.environment}"

  assume_role_policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17"
    Statement = [
      {
        Action = "sts:AssumeRole"
        Effect = "Allow"
        Principal = {
          Service = "ec2.amazonaws.com"
        }
      },
      {
        Action = "sts:AssumeRole"
        Effect = "Allow"
        Principal = {
          AWS = "arn:aws:iam::${data.aws_caller_identity.current.account_id}:root"
        }
        Condition = {
          StringEquals = {
            "sts:ExternalId" = var.external_id
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  })
}

# IAM Policy for Bedrock access (least privilege)
resource "aws_iam_role_policy" "bedrock_access" {
  name = "bedrock-access-policy"
  role = aws_iam_role.claude_code.id

  policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17"
    Statement = [
      {
        Sid    = "BedrockInvokeModel"
        Effect = "Allow"
        Action = [
          "bedrock:InvokeModel",
          "bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream"
        ]
        Resource = [
          "arn:aws:bedrock:${var.aws_region}::foundation-model/anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022-v2:0",
          "arn:aws:bedrock:${var.aws_region}::foundation-model/anthropic.claude-3-opus-20240229-v1:0",
          "arn:aws:bedrock:${var.aws_region}::foundation-model/anthropic.claude-3-haiku-20240307-v1:0"
        ]
      },
      {
        Sid    = "KMSDecrypt"
        Effect = "Allow"
        Action = [
          "kms:Decrypt",
          "kms:GenerateDataKey"
        ]
        Resource = aws_kms_key.bedrock.arn
      },
      {
        Sid    = "CloudWatchLogs"
        Effect = "Allow"
        Action = [
          "logs:CreateLogGroup",
          "logs:CreateLogStream",
          "logs:PutLogEvents"
        ]
        Resource = "${aws_cloudwatch_log_group.claude_code.arn}:*"
      },
      {
        Sid    = "SecretsManagerRead"
        Effect = "Allow"
        Action = [
          "secretsmanager:GetSecretValue"
        ]
        Resource = aws_secretsmanager_secret.api_keys.arn
      }
    ]
  })
}

# CloudWatch Log Group for auditing
resource "aws_cloudwatch_log_group" "claude_code" {
  name              = "/aws/claude-code/${var.environment}"
  retention_in_days = 90
  kms_key_id        = aws_kms_key.bedrock.arn
}

# Secrets Manager for API credentials
resource "aws_secretsmanager_secret" "api_keys" {
  name        = "claude-code/api-keys-${var.environment}"
  description = "API keys and credentials for Claude Code"
  kms_key_id  = aws_kms_key.bedrock.id

  rotation_rules {
    automatically_after_days = 90
  }
}

# CloudWatch Alarms for monitoring
resource "aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm" "bedrock_throttling" {

# Parte 3: Setup Script

## scripts/setup-bedrock.sh

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

ENVIRONMENT="${1:-prod}"
REGION="${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}"

echo "🚀 Setting up Claude Code with AWS Bedrock"
echo "Environment: $ENVIRONMENT"
echo "Region: $REGION"
echo ""

# 1. Deploy infrastructure
echo "📦 Deploying Terraform infrastructure..."
cd terraform/
terraform init
terraform plan -var="environment=$ENVIRONMENT" -out=tfplan
terraform apply tfplan

# Get outputs
ROLE_ARN=$(terraform output -raw iam_role_arn)
KMS_KEY=$(terraform output -raw kms_key_id)
VPC_ENDPOINT=$(terraform output -raw vpc_endpoint_id)
LOG_GROUP=$(terraform output -raw log_group_name)

echo "✅ Infrastructure deployed"
echo "  Role ARN: $ROLE_ARN"
echo "  KMS Key: $KMS_KEY"
echo "  VPC Endpoint: $VPC_ENDPOINT"
echo ""

# 2. Configure Claude Code
echo "⚙️  Configuring Claude Code..."

export AWS_ROLE_ARN="$ROLE_ARN"
export KMS_KEY_ID="$KMS_KEY"
export BEDROCK_VPC_ENDPOINT="https://vpce-${VPC_ENDPOINT}-bedrock-runtime.${REGION}.vpce.amazonaws.com"

# Substitute variables in config
envsubst < .claude/config-bedrock.json > ~/.config/claude-code/config.json

echo "✅ Claude Code configured"
echo ""

# 3. Test connection
echo "🧪 Testing Bedrock connection..."

claude --test-connection || {
  echo "❌ Connection test failed"
  exit 1
}

echo "✅ Connection test passed"
echo ""

# 4. Setup monitoring
echo "📊 Setting up monitoring dashboard..."

aws cloudwatch put-dashboard \
  --dashboard-name "ClaudeCode-Bedrock-${ENVIRONMENT}" \
  --dashboard-body file://monitoring/dashboard.json

echo "✅ Monitoring configured"
echo ""

echo "🎉 Setup complete!"
echo ""
echo "Next steps:"
echo "1. Test with: claude 'Explain this codebase'"
echo "2. View logs: aws logs tail $LOG_GROUP --follow"
echo "3. Monitor: https://console.aws.amazon.com/cloudwatch/home?region=$REGION#dashboards:"
```

# Parte 4: Runbook Operacional

## RUNBOOK.md

```markdown
# Claude Code + AWS Bedrock Runbook

## Health Checks

### Daily
```bash
# Check Bedrock availability
aws bedrock list-foundation-models --region us-east-1

# Check VPC endpoint status
aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --vpc-endpoint-ids $VPC_ENDPOINT_ID

# Check recent errors
aws logs filter-log-events \
  --log-group-name /aws/claude-code/prod \
  --start-time $(date -u -d '1 hour ago' +%s)000 \
  --filter-pattern "ERROR"
```

### Weekly
- Review CloudWatch alarms
- Check IAM access analyzer findings
- Review KMS key rotation status
- Analyze cost and usage

## Incident Response

### Scenario 1: High Error Rate

1. **Identify**:
   ```bash
   aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics \
     --namespace AWS/Bedrock \
     --metric-name ModelInvocationErrors \
     --start-time $(date -u -d '1 hour ago' +%s) \
     --end-time $(date -u +%s) \
     --period 300 \
     --statistics Sum
   ```

2. **Diagnose**:
   - Check CloudWatch logs for error messages
   - Verify IAM permissions
   - Check VPC endpoint connectivity
   - Verify model availability

3. **Remediate**:
   - If throttling: implement exponential backoff
   - If permissions: update IAM policy
   - If network: check security groups/NACLs

### Scenario 2: Security Incident

1. **Isolate**:
   ```bash
   # Revoke IAM role permissions immediately
   aws iam detach-role-policy \
     --role-name claude-code-bedrock-role-prod \
     --policy-arn $POLICY_ARN
   ```

2. **Investigate**:
   ```bash
   # Query CloudTrail for API calls
   aws cloudtrail lookup-events \
     --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=bedrock
   ```

3. **Recover**:
   - Rotate all credentials via Secrets Manager
   - Update security groups
   - Restore access with new IAM role

## Disaster Recovery

### RTO: 1 hour | RPO: 5 minutes

**Backup Strategy**:
- Terraform state: S3 with versioning
- Configs: Git repository
- Logs: CloudWatch with 90-day retention

**Recovery Steps**:
1. Restore Terraform state from S3
2. Re-run `terraform apply`
3. Restore configs from Git
4. Validate with test suite

## Cost Optimization

- Use Haiku model for simple tasks (90% cheaper)
- Implement request caching
- Set up budget alerts
- Monitor token usage per user/team
```

exercises.title: Seguridad y Compliance
exercises.instructions: Responde sobre seguridad y compliance en deployments empresariales de Claude Code.

questions.question: ¿Cuál es la mejor práctica para manejar API keys de Anthropic en entornos empresariales?
options: Hardcodear en archivos de configuración committeados
Usar Secrets Manager/Vault con rotación automática y acceso auditado
Compartirlas por Slack en canal privado
questions.explanation: En entornos enterprise, las API keys deben manejarse con: 1) Secrets management service (AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault), 2) Rotación automática, 3) Acceso auditado (quién accedió cuándo), 4) Encriptación at rest, 5) Least privilege access.

questions.question: Para cumplir con GDPR/HIPAA, ¿qué debe configurarse en Claude Code?
options: Data residency (región), encryption at rest/transit, audit logging, data retention policies
Nada especial, Claude Code es compliant por defecto
questions.explanation: Compliance GDPR/HIPAA requiere: 1) Data residency (mantener datos en región específica), 2) Encryption at rest y in transit, 3) Audit logging completo (quién accedió a qué datos), 4) Data retention policies (cuánto tiempo guardar logs), 5) Right to deletion, 6) Access controls estrictos.

questions.question: ¿Qué técnica previene que Claude Code accidentalmente exponga información sensible en logs?
options: Secret masking/redaction automática en logs y outputs
questions.explanation: Secret masking/redaction detecta y reemplaza automáticamente patrones sensibles (API keys, passwords, PII) en logs y outputs antes de escribirlos. Ejemplo: 'sk_live_abcd1234' → 'sk_live_****'. Se configura con regex patterns.

questions.question: En un entorno enterprise multi-tenant, ¿cómo se debe aislar el uso de Claude Code entre equipos?
options: No es necesario, todos comparten configuración
IAM roles separados, network isolation, separate billing accounts, audit trails por equipo
questions.explanation: Aislamiento multi-tenant requiere: 1) IAM roles/service accounts separados por equipo, 2) Network isolation (VPCs diferentes), 3) Separate billing/cost tracking, 4) Audit trails independientes, 5) Resource quotas por equipo, 6) Data isolation (no cross-contamination).

questions.question: ¿Qué debe incluirse en un security audit de Claude Code?
options: IAM permissions audit, network security review, data flow analysis, compliance verification, incident response testing
questions.explanation: Security audit completo debe incluir: 1) IAM audit (principio de least privilege), 2) Network security (firewalls, VPCs, endpoints), 3) Data flow analysis (dónde van los datos), 4) Compliance verification (GDPR, SOC2, etc.), 5) Incident response testing (simulacros), 6) Vulnerability scanning, 7) Access logs review.

exercises.title: Optimización de Costos y Tokens
exercises.instructions: Responde sobre estrategias de optimización de costos en uso de Claude Code.

questions.question: ¿Cuál es la estrategia MÁS efectiva para reducir costos de Claude Code sin sacrificar calidad?
options: Usar siempre el modelo más barato (Haiku)
Model routing: Haiku para tareas simples, Sonnet para complejas, Opus solo cuando sea crítico
Limitar el número de requests por usuario
questions.explanation: Model routing inteligente optimiza costos: Haiku ($0.25/MTok) para tareas simples (formatting, docs), Sonnet ($3/MTok) para la mayoría del trabajo, Opus ($15/MTok) solo para arquitectura crítica o debugging complejo. Esto puede reducir costos 60-80% vs usar siempre Sonnet.

questions.question: ¿Qué técnica reduce tokens sin perder contexto importante?
options: Eliminar todos los comentarios del código
Prompt compression: resumir contexto, usar embeddings para recuperación selectiva
questions.explanation: Prompt compression mantiene calidad mientras reduce tokens: 1) Resumir archivos grandes (pasar summary + solo secciones relevantes), 2) Usar embeddings para retrieval (solo incluir código relevante), 3) Incremental context (agregar contexto solo cuando necesario), 4) Deduplicate content.

questions.question: ¿Cómo se implementa caching efectivo en Claude Code para reducir tokens repetidos?
options: Usar Anthropic's prompt caching para contexto repetido (documentación, schemas) - reduce hasta 90% tokens
Guardar todas las respuestas en Redis
questions.explanation: Anthropic prompt caching permite marcar bloques de contexto (docs, schemas, código base) que se cachean server-side por 5min. Subsequent requests que usen mismo contexto solo pagan por nueva porción. Ejemplo: schema de 20K tokens cacheado se cobra solo 200 tokens en subsecuentes requests. Ahorro: hasta 90%.

questions.question: Para un equipo de 50 developers usando Claude Code, ¿qué métrica es MÁS importante monitorear?
options: Cost per developer per feature delivered (ROI)
questions.explanation: El ROI (cost per feature) es la métrica clave. Ejemplo: Si Claude Code cuesta $5000/mes pero el equipo entrega 2x features (equivalente a contratar 25 devs más a $200K/año), el ROI es 50:1. Métricas a trackear: cost/developer/month, features delivered, time saved, bug reduction.

questions.question: ¿Qué estrategia previene 'token waste' por errores o retries innecesarios?
options: Exponential backoff, input validation antes de llamar Claude, circuit breaker pattern
questions.explanation: Prevenir token waste: 1) Input validation (verificar que request es válido antes de enviar), 2) Exponential backoff (evitar spam de retries), 3) Circuit breaker (pausar si servicio está fallando), 4) Request deduplication (no enviar duplicados), 5) Timeout optimization (fallar fast si no responde).
